name: Hip Internal Rotation
definition: A strict unilateral open-chain hip isolation performed seated on a 75-cm hydraulic treatment table with both hips and knees held at 90 degrees, both feet suspended, the hands crossed over the shoulders, and the pelvis neutral. Bilateral anterior-superior-iliac-spine belts prevent associated pelvic and spinal motion, a distal-femur belt prevents non-rotational hip motion, and an ankle brace connects the working lower leg to the directly reviewed rotary-axis flywheel cable. The concentric phase internally rotates the femur relative to the fixed pelvis as fast as possible; the return counteracts the generated flywheel inertia. Lahuerta-Martín directly anchors this dynamic fixture and its measured force, power, and velocity, but measures no muscle activity. Gluteus medius and TFL are non-ranked co-primary contributors: Delp found every measured gluteus-medius compartment internally directed at 90 degrees, and Peduzzi de Castro directly measured both regions during a condition-matched internal-rotation effort without establishing a cross-muscle magnitude hierarchy. The unvisualized gluteus-minimus region is a mechanics-derived secondary because all measured compartments share the 90-degree internal-rotation direction; it earns exact-region analytics without a 3D surface. Piriformis is capable at this posture but remains unassigned: Delp reports a materially smaller 90-degree internal-rotation moment arm than the gluteus-minimus compartments, and no condition-matched source measured its recruitment. Obliques receive mechanics-derived stabilizer credit for the explicitly held spine and pelvis under flywheel torque; this is control credit, not measured EMG or rotation volume. Whole gluteus maximus receives no mover credit because its unsplit fibers do not share one rotation direction at this posture. Neutral-flexion, prone, standing, band, cable-stack, selectorized-machine, manual-resistance, unsupported, mobility, gait, pivoting, stepping, squat-control, pelvis-rotation, and combined hip-motion variants remain outside this contract.

exercises.name: Seated Flywheel Hip Internal Rotation
movementSteps: Sit on a hydraulic treatment table set 75 cm above the floor with both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees, both feet hanging freely, your hands crossed over your shoulders, and your pelvis centered.
Secure the lower end of the working thigh with one belt and place two belts across the front points of your hip bones to hold your pelvis still.

Connect the working ankle brace to the Conic Power Move cable with a carabiner. Set the wall-mounted flywheel 7 cm above the floor in the upper-middle frame position, attach the 460 g load 15 cm from the center, and adjust the cable so your hip can move through its full comfortable range.
Turn the working thigh inward as fast as possible so the lower leg moves outward while the pelvis stays still.
Return while resisting the flywheel's pull, keeping the knee angle fixed and avoiding movement through the pelvis or back.
Complete two sets of ten progressively harder warm-up repetitions, then perform three progressive repetitions and seven high-intensity work repetitions.
Repeat the same setup for the other leg and log it as a separate set.
